newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil trade says can't confirm Canada wheat deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil trade says can't confirm Canada wheat deal.

text.p: Brazilian traders said they had heard rumors that Canada sold around 500,000 tonnes of wheat to Brazil but they were unable to confirm the purchase.
North American grain trade sources said the Canadian Wheat Board (CWB) overnight sold 600,000 tonnes of wheat to Brazil at US$150/tonne FOB St. Lawrence for May-July delivery.

The sources said Brazilian milling group J. Macedo and a Bunge y Born subsidiary were the likely buyers, but an official at J. Macedo on Tuesday who declined to be named denied the firm had bought any Canadian wheat recently.

The J. Macedo official estimated Brazil would buy four million tonnes of Argentine wheat this year, with 1.5 million tonnes already shipped. A further 1.5 million tonnes from Argentina has also already been agreed, he added.
An official of Bunge unit Santista Alimentos said the firm could neither confirm nor deny the rumor.
But traders said Brazil may import more Canadian wheat than originally expected this year due to a drop in the quality of Argentine wheat after heavy rains during the harvest.

"There were rumours that half a million tonnes of Canadian wheat has been bought at around $150 a tonne," said Lawrence Pih at Moinho Pacifico. Brazil could import up to one million tonnes of Canadian wheat this year, Pih added.

"The quality for this current harvest is substantially below expectations and substantially below what it was at the same time last year. It is not suitable for baking. We will have to import Canadian wheat to blend with it," Pih said.
Canada supplied 375,000 tonnes of Brazil's wheat imports of 2.15 million tonnes between August and December, according to the Agriculture Ministry's National Supply Company (Conab).
A CWB official in November said Brazil bought 1.12 million tonnes of Canadian wheat last season but would probably buy half that amount in the current (Aug/July) crop year.

Argentina later said rains in Bahia Blanca and other regions had affected one million tonnes of total estimated wheat production of 15.5 million tonnes, with lower-quality wheat expected to be exported as feed-grade grain.
Antenor Barros Leal, president of the Brazilian Association of Wheat Industries (Abitrigo) which represents millers, said he was not aware of any additional problems with quality.
"We know that there are some parts of the Argentine wheat which have suffered from quality problems this year. One million tonnes of Argentine wheat has germinated," Leal said.
But Leal said complaints about quality were no higher, proportionally speaking, than last year. "There was a larger wheat harvest this year in Argentina," he said.
However, some Brazilian traders said they suspected wheat was being blended at origin with higher-quality product.
"They are blending it at the origin and when it arrives at the port FOB it has already been blended," said a trader.
"We haven't felt it much so far because exports are coming mainly from upriver. But as this wheat runs out and we start to import from ports in the south, the quality will drop," he said.
The differential between lower- and higher-quality Argentine wheat was between $8 and $10 a tonne. "In a normal year, you wouldn't have this spread," he added.
